description: Bare, blotched, hairless and shaped exactly like a person, coming at a walk with one hand open and green.
lore: Out on the black rock, where the ground is warm underfoot, something walks that is exactly the shape of a person. Bare, hairless, not a stitch on it, the head a little large for the body, skin blotched in patches that do not match one another. Nothing about it is monstrous in the way that word usually goes. The masked ones drop a face in the dirt when they go down; this one never took the face off, and wears the whole thing, all over, all the time.

It kept the belongings too, and that is the part people find hard. A bronze locket knotted over with spirals, worn in under the skin. A pitted silver band still sitting on a finger, plainly never made for that hand. Grave dirt worked into the creases. A bundle of long pale bones on a cord, carried. Half a spool of plain linen thread. Every one of those is a fact about somebody with the somebody taken out of it, and the people who go through what one of these leaves behind are not robbing it so much as reading it. No name has ever been read off one.

It follows, and it does not hurry. Upright, arms hanging and never swinging, which is what tells you at fifty paces, because a person's arms swing and this one's do not. When it arrives it does not bite and it does not claw. It reaches. An open hand, out and across, a gesture anybody would recognise, and everyone who has met one says that is the worse thing. What comes off the hand is green. There is green in the seams of it under the blotching, and by every account it is what holds the shape upright now; where the skin has parted it weeps. It does not clear out of a wound. It settles, and the next one settles on top of that, and the next on top of that again. Nothing about this creature ever subtracts.

Why the outside is the part that lasted has a tidy account, and the people fondest of it are the ones who have not been out there. It runs like this: the outside of a person is the part other people hold — a face, a build, the set of a hand doing nothing, kept by every acquaintance who ever passed it in a doorway — while the inside was only ever held by the one occupant. That is a decent account of skin still walking and no account at all of the rest. Not of what did the taking. Not of why it went all at once instead of over an age. Not of why it is happening now, and here, on ground where none of this used to happen. Break one and it puts its hands down first, the way something might that half remembers kneeling, then folds up small, and the colour washes out of it, blotches and flush and all, until there is a pale heap on the warm rock getting flatter. The stone is in there: cobbled grey, green still leaking from every joint of it, warm in the palm, and warm and leaking in a hundred years. Harder to put down is where the heap was. A long way round the massif from any way into the cave that anybody knows, and it was not out there on its own.
